extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for founders on when to engage press, how to craft pitches, how to approach different tiers of media, and how to run crisis communications. Emphasizes founder-owned narrative, quality over quantity, and a short pitch template.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founders own the narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Founders own the narrative — not the firm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principle that founders should control messaging and public narrative rather than letting investors or others speak for the company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality matters more than quantity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize high-quality, newsworthy outreach over frequent, low-value coverage. One meaningful placement is preferred to many superficial mentions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term relationships beat short-term coverage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in building enduring relationships with reporters and outlets rather than transactional, one-off hits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be different, not loud
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for distinctiveness and substance in messaging instead of attention-seeking or volume-based tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Let your work speak first
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize building a strong product/business narrative and demonstrable results; coverage should follow meaningful progress or evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Series A+ funding rounds (When to Engage — Always)
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed under 'Always' — Series A+ funding rounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag for press engagement: when the company reaches significant financing milestones (Series A and beyond).

rubrics_metrics.name: Major product launches that change capability (When to Engage — Always)
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed under 'Always' — Major product launches that change capability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage press for launches that materially change what the product can do or the market landscape.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant customer wins (Fortune 500 logos) (When to Engage — Always)
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed under 'Always' — Significant customer wins (Fortune 500 logos).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large, credible customer acquisitions validate market traction and warrant media outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry-shifting data reports (When to Engage — Always)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish and pitch original data or reports that change industry conversations; these are newsworthy events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis communication (When to Engage — Always)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any crisis requires immediate communications engagement and follows the crisis protocol (designated spokesperson, facts-only, investor notification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notable hires (When to Engage — Sometimes)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage when hires bring significant credibility, name recognition, or strategic change; otherwise avoid routine hire announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic partnerships with major players (When to Engage — Sometimes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed under 'Sometimes' — Strategic partnerships with major players.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicize partnerships that materially affect distribution, product capability, or market perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards from credible bodies (When to Engage — Sometimes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed under 'Sometimes' — Awards from credible bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selective award coverage can be useful if the awarding body is respected and the recognition is meaningful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference keynote opportunities (When to Engage — Sometimes)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use high-visibility speaking slots to tell a broader narrative; pitch around them when the speaker/content is especially newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor product updates (When to Engage — Almost Never)
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed under 'Almost Never' — Minor product updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid pitching small incremental changes as news; they dilute credibility if overused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal milestones (When to Engage — Almost Never)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid promoting internal company events or operational milestones that lack external impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Junior hires (When to Engage — Almost Never)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not pitch routine, non-strategic hires; reserve coverage for senior leadership or uniquely notable hires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay-to-play awards (When to Engage — Almost Never)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid publicizing awards that are effectively purchased or lack independent credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic thought leadership (When to Engage — Almost Never)
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed under 'Almost Never' — Generic thought leadership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generic opinion pieces without distinctive data, perspective, or news hook are unlikely to earn meaningful coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: a16z Pitch Template (Subject line + Body structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject Line: "[News in 6-8 words] — [Why specific reporter]". Body: Para 1: The news (specific, concrete); Para 2: Why it matters in your beat; Para 3: What I can offer (interview, demo, exclusive, data); Sign-off: Founder name, phone, calendar link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep subject lines short and reporter-specific; open with the concrete news, explain relevance to the reporter's beat, offer tangible interview/demo/exclusive options, and end with clear contact/availability information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitching Tier 1 — Major Outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: Tier 1 — Major Outlets (NYT, WSJ, Bloomberg): Embargoed exclusive only; Founder available immediately; 2 days advance notice minimum; Customer references ready; Investor reference ready.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For top-tier outlets, prefer exclusives under embargo, ensure founder availability on short notice, and have customer and investor references prepared to validate claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitching Tier 2 — Trade Press
rubrics_metrics.description: Tier 2 — Trade Press (TechCrunch, Information, Axios): Coordinated release; Multiple sources offered; Demo video pre-recorded; Press kit comprehensive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide coordinated materials and multiple sources; pre-record demos and assemble a thorough press kit to make reporting easier and more accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitching Tier 3 — Newsletters and Podcasts
rubrics_metrics.description: Tier 3 — Newsletters and Podcasts: Founder availability flexible; Conversational format; Specific story angle; Audience-fit demonstrated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For newsletters/podcasts, emphasize a clear story angle, demonstrate fit with audience, and be flexible about founder scheduling and conversational formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis Communication Protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Notify investors within hours; Brief response team; Single spokesperson designated; Specific facts only — no speculation; Update cadence specified; Long-form context piece if needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a crisis, act quickly: inform investors, activate a small response team, use a single authorized spokesperson, limit public statements to verified facts, set a schedule for updates, and consider a longer-form contextual communication once immediate facts are controlled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worth-doing test passed (Quality Rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A potential PR effort should pass a gut/strategic test that the news is genuinely worth publicizing — it must be substantive and meaningful to audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founder owns narrative (Quality Rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinforces the principle that the founder should be the primary voice and steward of external messaging; investors/PR should support but not supplant the founder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier-appropriate distribution (Quality Rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose distribution and pitching tactics appropriate to the story's significance and the target outlet tier (e.g., exclusive vs. coordinated release).

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalized pitches (Quality Rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid mass, generic outreach; tailor subject lines and pitch angles to the specific reporter and outlet to increase relevance and pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer + investor proof points (Quality Rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support claims with credible references such as notable customers or investors to provide external validation for news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honest, specific claims (Quality Rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make only verifiable, specific claims; avoid exaggeration or vague marketing language that can be challenged by reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis protocol if needed (Quality Rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure there is a defined crisis protocol to be activated in case of emergencies — includes investor notification, designated spokesperson, facts-only messaging, and update cadence.
